subject: Request: latency carveout and service-credit cap for Undertow (UW-5934)
messages:
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@undertow.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@undertow.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SLO carveout & cap (UW-5934)

Hi Connor —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re close on the commercial terms but one technical issue has popped up on our side that will require a non-standard SLO concession for the first 6 months after go-live. Short version: the model flavor we want to run in our private VPC has an intermittent cold-start pattern during peak ingest windows which spikes tail latency for a small subset of requests.

What we’re asking for:
- Allow a reduced uptime/latency SLA for that non-critical variant (target 99.5% uptime for the first 6 months vs standard 99.9%).
- Limit remedies: cap service credits to 5% of monthly invoice instead of Redwood’s standard uncapped or 10% formulations.
- In exchange we’re asking for a first-year onboarding discount and that Redwood include the latency remediation plan as an appendix to the contract.

I’ve attached our internal latency analysis and a short note on request distribution. Can you confirm if this is something Redwood can approve or if you need exec sign-off / deal desk? We’re trying to close procurement by month end.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramirez
Head of Platform, Undertow.ai
sofia@undertow.ai
Attachment: uptime-analysis.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: SLO carveout & cap (UW-5934)

Looping you both in — forwarding Undertow’s ask (below). They want a temporary latency/uptime carveout for a non-critical model variant and a hard cap on credits at 5%, plus a first-year discount in exchange. Procurement wants an answer this month.

My read: this is a classic deal-desk escalation — small commercial concession in return for a controlled risk profile and an explicit remediation plan. Marissa, can you propose an approval path and recommended commercial tradeoff? Lauren / Vivek — please weigh in on executive guardrails if you see any non-negotiables (e.g., language we should never accept).

Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai

> > Hi Connor —
> >
> > Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re close on the commercial terms but one technical issue has popped up on our side that will require a non-standard SLO concession for the first 6 months after go-live...
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Request: SLO carveout & cap (UW-5934)

Thanks for the context — reviewed Undertow’s analysis and pulled numbers with Finance. High level recommendation:

- Approve a timeboxed SLO: 99.5% uptime for the specified non-critical variant for 6 months post-go-live.
- Remedy cap: Agree to a hard cap on service credits at 5% of the monthly invoice (per month). No aggregate uncapped exposure.
- Commercial trade: 12% off list for the first 12 months on the Dedicated commit (we can structure as a usage credit to keep bookings intact).
- Contract language: Include a remediation appendix that defines (a) the impacted model variant, (b) the specific metrics and measurement windows, and (c) a 6-month review clause with telemetry share.

Why this is acceptable: 1) The carveout is limited in scope and duration, 2) the credit cap bounds financial exposure, and 3) the review clause gives us an instrument to revert to standard SLA if problems persist.

Action items:
- Connor to confirm Undertow accepts the 12% trade (they asked for 15%).
- Legal to prepare term-sheet redlines with the exact remedy cap and appendix language (I’ve attached a draft term sheet).
- Engineering to add route tags and monitoring dashboard for the variant so we can measure the review metrics.

Attaching: redwood_slo_term_sheet.pdf (term language + suggested appendix)

Marissa Cole
Director, Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood_slo_term_sheet.pdf (pdf)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T13:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: SLO carveout & cap (UW-5934)

I’ve reviewed Marissa’s recommendation and the attachments. I’m comfortable approving the concession with the following required conditions:

1) Approve 99.5% uptime for the named non-critical variant, duration 6 months from go-live.
2) Approve remedy cap: 5% of monthly invoice, measured and applied per monthly billing period (explicitly no uncapped exposure).
3) Commercial adjustment: approve 12% first-year credit as Marissa proposed (not 15%).
4) Add mandatory audit clause: Undertow must provide Redwood with the specified telemetry and allow a quarterly ops review during the carveout window.
5) Add a rollback trigger: if the variant causes customer-visible outages or repeated SLA breaches (>=2 months in the 6-month window), Redwood may revert the account to standard terms and remove the credit.

Please have Legal incorporate the exact remedy cap language: “SLA remedy payments shall not exceed five percent (5%) of the Customer’s monthly Redwood invoice in any given monthly billing period.” Also insert a clause requiring an operations review at month 3.

Lauren — approve the final redline and notify sales once Legal posts the DocuSign. Connor — if you get buyer acceptance, get Michael Chen (procurement) on a brief call so we can nail the sign-off and timeline.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@undertow.ai>, Michael Chen <michael.chen@undertow.ai>

Date: 2027-04-13T16:24:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: Undertow SLO carveout (UW-5934)

Hi Sofia / Michael —

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed this internally. Executive summary of what Redwood will commit to:

- Temporary SLO: 99.5% uptime for the identified non-critical model variant for 6 months from production go-live.
- Remedy cap: Service credits (SLA remedies) capped at 5% of the monthly invoice, measured per billing period.
- Commercial: 12% onboarding credit applied to first 12 months.
- Conditions: Undertow to provide telemetry access for the variant, participate in a 3-month ops review, and agree to a rollback trigger if repeated breaches occur.

Attached is the updated term sheet with legal redlines and a DocuSign link for signature. Proposed timeline: we can have the signed paperwork in 5 business days and target a go-live two weeks after signature to allow engineering changes.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/terminate/UW-5934-term-sheet
Attachment: redwood_slo_term_sheet.pdf

If that works, Michael — can you confirm procurement will accept 12% (they asked for 15%) and sign the DocuSign by end of next week? If you want a quick alignment call I’m available tomorrow 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
Connor O’Brien
